transcript.text: hi, we keep losing customers every month and i dont know what to do about it

I can help. If you have a customer file with churn or cancellation dates, that’s ideal. Pick the option that best matches what you need — whether it’s understanding the cause, catching at-risk customers early, or building a retention plan.

choices.title: Find out why customers are leaving
choices.what: Compare customers who churned with those who stayed, using the data you already have. You get: The main reasons, patterns, or customer types behind monthly losses. Trade-off: Needs enough historical data with a clear churn indicator. Effort: Medium.

choices.title: Flag likely churners before they leave
choices.what: Build a model that scores each current customer for risk of leaving next month. You get: A targeted list of customers to try to retain. Trade-off: Needs customer-level history and a defined outcome such as 'churned within 30/60/90 days'. Effort: Higher.

choices.title: Get a practical retention plan
choices.what: Turn what you know about the problem into recommended actions, priorities, and likely impact. You get: A business-style brief on what to do first and how to measure whether it works. Trade-off: May rely on assumptions if the data is limited. Effort: Lower.

transcript.text: 2. i want the list of people to call before they leave, not the deep reasons.

I’ve started the churn-warning project.

To build it, please upload or point me to a customer table. Useful fields include:

- Customer ID
- Churn status or cancellation date
- Subscription start date
- Last activity or usage date
- Monthly usage, spend, plan type, support tickets
- Any customer details that might matter

If you can also tell me how you define “churn” — for example, no activity for 30, 60, or 90 days — I can use that as the target.

choices.title: Predictive churn report
choices.what: Build a model that scores each member’s chance of cancelling next month, then create a weekly report of the highest-risk members. You get: A model-based risk ranking updated weekly. Trade-off: Requires checking that each record has a reliable outcome label and enough history. Effort: Medium.

choices.title: Rule-based risk list
choices.what: Use observable patterns now, such as low tenure, low spend, or recent support tickets, to list likely cancellations each week. You get: A quick report without building a predictive model. Trade-off: Less personalized and may miss combined signals. Effort: Low.

choices.title: Model + campaign list
